description: The chart represents the distribution of four categories across three difficulty levels: easy, medium, and hard. Each pie chart is divided into four slices, representing the categories N+K+, N-K+, N-K-, and N+K-. The easy chart has slices labeled with percentages: N+K+ (teal, 40.6%), N-K+ (beige, 45.9%), N-K- (orange, 10.1%), and N+K- (red, 3.3%). The medium chart also has labeled slices: N+K+ (teal, 44.6%), N-K+ (beige, 44.3%), N-K- (orange, 7.2%), and N+K- (red, 3.9%). The hard chart has labeled slices: N+K+ (teal, 36.2%), N-K+ (beige, 20.1%), N-K- (orange, 36.7% with a small gray section within it, labeled 7.0%), and N+K- (red, not directly labeled but can be inferred as the remaining proportion). A legend on the right side of the chart indicates the color corresponding to each category. The charts do not have visually emphasized slices, but the categories are consistently colored across the three charts. The proportions of the slices vary across the three difficulty levels, with the easy and medium charts having similar distributions, while the hard chart has a different distribution.
